mainTopic: Deposits with a שולחני, בעל הבית, or חנווני: when the keeper may use the money and when he pays for loss or אונס. Then how much a שומר pays after misusing a deposit.
overview: This amud opens with the last line of the previous case. A new משנה then teaches that a שולחני may use deposited money only if it is untied, and that if he may use it, he must pay if it is lost. A בעל הבית may never use it, and רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue whether a חנווני is like a בעל הבית or like a שולחני. The גמרא explains that tied money must also be sealed, or according to רב מארי tied with an unusual knot. In another version, רב מארי asks whether an unusual knot is enough and the question stays unresolved. רב הונא says the שולחני pays even for אונס, and רב נחמן disagrees. רב נחמן explains to רבא that the chance to profit makes the שולחני a שומר שכר. רב נחמן also challenges רב הונא from a משנה about a גזבר, and רב הונא answers that the wording 'he spent it' only matches the first part of that משנה. A second משנה brings three opinions on how much a שומר pays after misusing a deposit. The גמרא brings רבה's rule about a stolen barrel of wine, then shows that reading בית הלל's 'time of removal' as the time the item is destroyed does not work.

steps.title: Closing line of the previous case: paying for the hops
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the previous discussion: he pays the other person the value of the hops.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he pays him the value of the hops.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the final line of the discussion that came before our new משנה. It finishes that earlier case by saying he pays for the hops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line belongs to the earlier topic, not to the new משנה about deposits. It tells us how the earlier case ends: with a payment for the value of the hops.

keyTerms.meaning: The value of / the price of

phrases.english: And he pays him the value of the hops.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the sugya from the previous daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the earlier case, he pays the value of the hops.

steps.title: Money deposited with a money changer or a homeowner
steps.stepSummary: The משנה: a שולחני may use untied money and must pay if it is lost, but he may not use tied money and is not responsible for it. A בעל הבית may never use deposited money.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone deposits money with a money changer: if it is tied up, he may not use it, so if it is lost he is not responsible. If it is untied, he may use it, so if it is lost he is responsible. If it was deposited with a homeowner, whether tied or untied, he may not use it, so if it is lost he is not responsible.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches whether the person holding the money may use it, and whether he must pay if it is lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is לפיכך (therefore): being allowed to use the money is what makes the keeper responsible for losses. A שולחני deals in money, so if the money is left untied he may use it. A regular בעל הבית is never assumed to have permission, so tied or untied makes no difference for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Responsibility to pay for a loss
A regular homeowner (not a money professional)

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the basic rule of this sugya: permission to use a deposit brings responsibility for it.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who deposits money with a money changer,
if it is tied up, he may not use it,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ אִם אָבְדוּ אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתָן.
phrases.english: therefore, if it is lost, he is not responsible for it.
If it is untied, he may use it,
therefore, if it is lost, he is responsible for it.

phrases.aramaic: אֵצֶל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, בֵּין צְרוּרִין וּבֵין מוּתָּרִין –
phrases.english: If it was left with a homeowner, whether tied or untied,
he may not use it,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ אִם אָבְדוּ אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתָן.
phrases.english: therefore, if it is lost, he is not responsible for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שולחני may use untied deposited money and is then responsible for it. He may not use tied money and is not responsible for it. A בעל הבית may use neither and is not responsible.

steps.title: Is a storekeeper like a homeowner or a money changer?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says a חנווני is like a בעל הבית. רבי יהודה says he is like a שולחני.
steps.simpleTranslation: A storekeeper is like a homeowner; these are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: a storekeeper is like a money changer.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a disagreement about a storekeeper, who falls somewhere between a homeowner and a money changer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, a חנווני may never use deposited money, just like a בעל הבית. According to רבי יהודה, he follows the rules of the שולחני: untied money may be used, and he is then responsible for it.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three kinds of keepers: שולחני (may use untied money), בעל הבית (may never use it), and חנווני (disputed).

phrases.aramaic: חֶנְוָנִי כְּבַעַל הַבַּיִת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: A storekeeper is like a homeowner; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says: a storekeeper is like a money changer.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֶנְוָנִי כְּבַעַל הַבַּיִת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a disputed in-between case to the משנה's rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: a חנווני follows the rules of a בעל הבית. רבי יהודה: a חנווני follows the rules of a שולחני.

steps.title: Why should tying the money stop the money changer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: people normally tie up their money, so why should tying it mean he may not use it?
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Just because it is tied up, he may not use it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the משנה's first rule. It is setting up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lots of people tie their money just to carry it, so tying alone does not clearly show that the owner objects to its use. The גמרא wants to know what in the case shows the owner does not want the money touched.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Just because / because of the fact that

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ מִשּׁוּם דִּצְרוּרִין לֹא יִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן?
phrases.english: GEMARA: Just because it is tied up, he may not use it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first rule of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that tied money may not be used by a שולחני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tying is ordinary and does not show that the owner objects to the money being used.

steps.title: The money was tied and also sealed
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי in the name of רב יהודה: the משנה is talking about money that was tied and sealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said in the name of רב יהודה: the משנה was taught about money that was tied and sealed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by narrowing the case. 'Tied' in the משנה means tied and also sealed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A seal clearly shows that the owner does not want the bundle opened. So the שולחני may not use it. Plain tying without a seal would not be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught (the משנה was taught about this)

steps.confusionAlert: רב יהודה here is an אמורא quoted by רב אסי. He is not the same person as רבי יהודה, the תנא in the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Asi said that Rav Yehuda said:
They taught this about money that is tied and sealed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Plain tying would be enough to forbid using the money.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means money that was tied and sealed, which clearly shows the owner does not want it opened.

steps.title: The money was tied with an unusual knot
steps.stepSummary: רב מארי gives another answer: the משנה is talking about money tied with an unusual knot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מארי said: it is about money tied with an unusual knot.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to the same question. Instead of a seal, an unusual knot shows the owner does not want the money used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מארי holds that no seal is needed. A special knot also signals that the owner wants the bundle left closed, and that is enough to forbid using it.

phrases.english: Rav Mari says: it is with an unusual knot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to step 5's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a seal would show that the owner objects.
steps.terutzMaskana: An unusual knot is also enough to show the owner does not want the money used.

steps.title: Another version: רב מארי asks about the unusual knot
steps.stepSummary: Some say רב מארי did not rule; he asked what the law is for an unusual knot. The question stays unanswered (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who say: רב מארי asked, what is the law of an unusual knot? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a second version of רב מארי's words. In this version he asked a question instead of giving an answer, and the question is left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, it is unclear whether an unusual knot counts like a seal. Since no answer is found, the question ends with תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question stays unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the first, רב מארי rules that an unusual knot works. In the second, it is an open question.

phrases.english: There are those who say: Rav Mari asked:
An unusual knot, what is the law? Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of step 6, turning רב מארי's answer into a question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does an unusual knot count like a seal, so that the שולחני may not use the money?
steps.whatToRemember: A seal clearly forbids using the money. An unusual knot is either enough (first version) or an open question (second version).

steps.title: רב הונא: he must pay even for things beyond his control
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה's rule about untied money, רב הונא says the שולחני is responsible even for אונס.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If it is untied, he may use it,' and so on. רב הונא said: and even if it was taken by circumstances beyond his control.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, and רב הונא explains how far the שולחני's responsibility goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the שולחני is allowed to use the money, רב הונא says he must pay even when the loss was not his fault at all. This goes further than the plain word 'lost' in the משנה might suggest.

keyTerms.meaning: Were lost through אונס, circumstances beyond his control

phrases.english: 'If it is untied, he may use it,' etc.
Rav Huna said: and even if it was taken by circumstances beyond his control.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּתָּרִין יִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן כּוּ׳. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the משנה's second rule (untied money).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שולחני who may use the money must pay even for אונס.

steps.title: But the משנה only says 'lost'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא: the משנה says 'lost', which sounds like ordinary loss, not אונס.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches 'lost'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא from the משנה's own wording. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Lost' sounds like the keeper was careless. That suggests he pays only for that kind of loss and not for אונס, which would contradict רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches (a challenge from the wording)

phrases.english: But it teaches 'lost'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's statement that the שולחני pays even for אונס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says only 'lost', which suggests a loss that is not אונס.

steps.title: 'Lost' can mean even a sunken ship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רבה's teaching: 'stolen' can mean by armed bandits, and 'lost' can mean the ship sank at sea. Both are אונס.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רבה's teaching. For רבה said: 'They were stolen' means by armed bandits. 'They were lost' means his ship sank at sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by showing that the word 'lost' can include losses beyond a person's control.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה taught elsewhere that 'lost' can describe a ship sinking at sea, which is clearly אונס. So the משנה's word 'lost' fits רב הונא's ruling that the שולחני pays even for אונס.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא, a שולחני who may use untied money pays for its loss, even through אונס, because 'lost' can include a ship sinking at sea. רב נחמן disagrees in the next step.

phrases.english: It is like Rabba's teaching, as Rabba said:
'They were stolen' means by armed bandits,
'they were lost' means his ship sank at sea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Lost' means only a loss that is not אונס.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבה, 'lost' includes even a ship sinking at sea, which is אונס, so רב הונא's ruling fits the משנה.

steps.title: רב נחמן: The money changer does not pay for unavoidable accidents
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן disagrees with רב הונא and rules that the שולחני is not liable when untied money is lost through אונס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן says: if the money was lost through something beyond his control, he does not pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion on the same question רב הונא answered. רב נחמן says the שולחני does not pay for אונס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא treated the שולחני like a borrower, who pays even for accidents. רב נחמן disagrees and says he does not pay for אונס. He is still responsible for ordinary loss, as the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: They were lost through אונס, something beyond his control
An unavoidable accident, like armed robbers or a sinking ship

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman says:
If they were lost through an unavoidable accident, no [he does not pay].
phrases.notes: He is disagreeing with רב הונא from step 8, who said the שולחני pays even for אונס.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing opinion to רב הונא's ruling from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שולחני holding untied money is not liable for אונס.

steps.title: רבא asks: If he is not a borrower, how is he a paid guardian?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן: if the שולחני is not a שואל, he should not be a שומר שכר either, so why does he pay for loss?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: According to you, who says he does not pay for אונס, he is clearly not a borrower of the money. But if he is not a borrower, he is not a paid guardian either!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן's position. If the שולחני is not treated as a borrower, what makes him a paid guardian who pays for loss?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes the שולחני pay when untied money is lost, and only a שומר שכר pays for ordinary loss. A paid guardian is someone who gets something in return. רבא's point is that the שולחני got nothing except permission to use the money. If that permission does not make him a borrower, it should not make him a paid guardian either, so he should be only an unpaid guardian.

keyTerms.meaning: A borrower, who pays even for אונס
A paid guardian, who pays for theft and loss but not for אונס

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
According to you, who said that if they were lost through an accident he does not pay,
it turns out he is not a borrower of them;
if he is not a borrower,
he is not a paid guardian either!
phrases.notes: This is a problem because the משנה makes him pay when the money is lost, and only a paid guardian pays for that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: לְדִידָךְ דְּאָמְרַתְּ נֶאֶנְסוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's ruling from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that the שולחני is not liable for אונס but is liable for loss.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Permission to use the money either makes him a borrower or gives him nothing. If he is not a borrower, nothing is left to make him a paid guardian.

steps.title: רב נחמן: The chance for a good deal makes him a paid guardian
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the שולחני gets a real benefit, because he can use the money if a profitable deal comes up. That benefit makes him a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: On this point I agree with you that he is a paid guardian. Since he gets some benefit, namely that if a profitable purchase comes his way he can buy with this money, he is a paid guardian over it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends himself. He explains what the שולחני gains, and that gain makes him a paid guardian.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being ready to grab a good deal is a real benefit, even if he never actually spends the money. That benefit is enough to make him a שומר שכר, who pays for loss. It is not enough to make him a borrower, who pays even for אונס.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, the שולחני with untied money is a שומר שכר: he pays for loss but not for אונס, because his benefit is only the chance to use the money.

phrases.english: He said to him: On this point I agree with you,
that since he gets some benefit,
through that benefit,
that if a purchase happens to come his way
that has profit in it, he can buy with them,
he is a paid guardian over them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a middle level of benefit that creates paid-guardian status without borrower status.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא thought permission to use the money made him either a borrower or nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ready chance to profit is a benefit that makes him a שומר שכר but not a שואל.

steps.title: רב נחמן quotes a משנה about a Temple treasurer's deposit
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges רב הונא by quoting a משנה from מסכת מעילה. If a גזבר deposits tied money and the שולחני spends it, the גזבר is not guilty of מעילה. If the money was untied, the גזבר is guilty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן challenged רב הונא from a משנה: If someone deposits money with a money changer, and it is tied up, the money changer may not use it. So if he spent it, the treasurer did not commit מעילה. If it is untied, the money changer may use it. So if he spent it, the treasurer did commit מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן opens an attack on רב הונא by quoting a משנה. This step only sets up the source; the actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With untied money, the שולחני is allowed to spend it, so he acts on behalf of the גזבר. That makes the גזבר guilty of misusing הקדש money. With tied money, the שולחני had no permission, so the misuse is his own and not the גזבר's. Notice that the משנה ties the גזבר's guilt to the moment the money is spent.

keyTerms.meaning: Treasurer of the בית המקדש funds
Committed מעילה, misuse of הקדש property

phrases.english: Rav Nachman challenged Rav Huna:
One who deposits money with a money changer,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מעילה 21b, about a גזבר depositing money that belongs to הקדש.

phrases.english: if it is tied up, he may not use it;

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ אִם הוֹצִיא – לֹא מָעַל הַגִּזְבָּר.
phrases.english: therefore, if he spent it, the treasurer did not commit misuse.
And if it is untied, he may use it;
therefore, if he spent it, the treasurer committed misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רב נחמן's own defense and turns to attack רב הונא's ruling from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that the שולחני pays even for אונס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: the משנה links the treasurer's guilt to the spending. The next step explains why this contradicts רב הונא.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need the money to be spent?
steps.stepSummary: If the שולחני pays even for אונס, the money is already like a loan once it is deposited. Then the גזבר should be guilty right away, even before anything is spent.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he pays even for an accident, why does the משנה specifically say 'he spent it'? Even if he did not spend it, the treasurer should be guilty too!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן now spells out his question. He shows why the משנה's wording does not fit רב הונא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שולחני is responsible even for אונס, he holds the money like a borrower from the moment he receives it. The money has then already left הקדש's control, so the גזבר's misuse should happen at the handover. The משנה's words 'if he spent it' suggest that this is not so.

phrases.english: And if you say [he pays] even if they were lost through an accident,
why specifically 'he spent it'?
Even if he did not spend it, too!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ אֲפִילּוּ נֶאֶנְסוּ, מַאי אִירְיָא הוֹצִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the משנה quoted in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that the שולחני pays even for אונס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Liability for אונס means the money counts as a loan at the moment of deposit. Then the treasurer's misuse should not depend on the spending, yet the משנה says 'if he spent it'.

steps.title: רב הונא: 'He spent it' just matches the first part of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the גזבר is guilty even if nothing was spent. The משנה says 'he spent it' in the second part only to match the first part.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The same law applies even if he did not spend it. But since the first part of the משנה said 'he spent it,' the last part also said 'he spent it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends his view. He explains that the word 'spent' in the second part of the משנה is just a matter of style.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first part, with tied money, spending is really needed: only then does the שולחני misuse the money. The משנה kept the same word in the second part for parallel wording, but there the גזבר is guilty from the handover. So the משנה does not contradict רב הונא, and his ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because the משנה already used this wording
The first part / the last part of a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא keeps his ruling that the שולחני pays even for אונס. The משנה's word 'spent' in the second part is only there to match the first part.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as רב הונא changing his mind. He fully agrees the treasurer is guilty even without spending; he only explains why the משנה used that word.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא answering רב נחמן.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא הוֹצִיא,
phrases.english: The same law applies even though he did not spend it,
and since the first part taught 'he spent it,'
the last part also taught 'he spent it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הוּא הַדִּין אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא הוֹצִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge from steps 14 and 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: איידי: the wording of the second part copies the first part for parallel style.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'spent' in the second part seemed to mean the treasurer's guilt depends on spending.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word is only for parallel style. The treasurer is guilty from the handover, which fits רב הונא's view that the שולחני pays even for אונס.

steps.title: The משנה: three opinions on paying for a misused deposit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a מחלוקת about a שומר who misuses a deposit. בית שמאי make him pay whichever value is worse for him. בית הלל say he pays by its value at the time of removal. רבי עקיבא says he pays by its value at the time of the claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: If someone misuses a deposit, בית שמאי say: he loses out whether it went down or up in value. בית הלל say: he pays by its value at the time he took it out. רבי עקיבא says: he pays by its value at the time the owner claims it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It asks how much a שומר pays once he has wrongly used the item he was guarding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the שומר misuses the deposit, he is treated like a thief, so he becomes responsible for it. The question is which moment sets the price. בית שמאי pick the worst value for him, בית הלל pick the 'time of removal,' and רבי עקיבא pick the time the owner comes to claim it.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'sends a hand.' It means wrongly using or taking something you were only supposed to guard.
A deposit, an item given to someone to watch
The time the owner makes his claim

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the סוגיא keeps trying to work out what בית הלל mean by 'time of removal.'

phrases.english: MISHNA
One who misappropriates a deposit
Beit Shammai say
He is penalized for decrease and for increase
And Beit Hillel say
According to the time of removal
Rabbi Akiva says
According to the time of the claim

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the שולחני and גזבר discussion in steps 2-16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר who misuses a deposit pays by the worst value (בית שמאי), by the value at the time of removal (בית הלל), or by the value at the time of the claim (רבי עקיבא).

steps.title: רבה's case of the stolen barrel that rose in value
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules about a robber who stole a barrel of wine worth one זוז that later became worth four. If he broke it or drank it, he pays four. If it broke on its own, he pays one.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רבה says: Someone stole a barrel of wine from his friend. At first it was worth one זוז, and now it is worth four. If he broke it or drank it, he pays four. If it broke by itself, he pays one זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a rule from רבה about a stolen item whose price went up while the robber had it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount the robber pays depends on how the barrel was destroyed. If he destroyed it himself, he pays the new, higher price. If it broke by itself, he pays only the price from when he stole it.
steps.confusionAlert: Even though it is the same barrel and the same robber, the payment changes based on who broke it. Keep the two cases separate.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabba says
This one who robbed
a barrel of wine from his friend
at first it was worth a zuz
now it is worth four
if he broke it or drank it
he pays four
if it broke by itself
he pays a zuz

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה הַאי מַאן דִּגְזַל חָבִיתָא דְחַמְרָא מֵחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related rule about a robber's payment. Later steps will test it against the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A robber who destroys the stolen item himself pays its current value. If it breaks by itself, he pays its value at the time of the robbery.

steps.title: Why breaking or drinking it costs four
steps.stepSummary: While the barrel is still whole, the robber simply gives it back as it is. So the moment he breaks or drinks it counts as a new act of stealing. The משנה teaches that robbers pay by the value at the time of the robbery, and at that moment the barrel was worth four.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? If the barrel were still there, it would go back to its owner as it is. So the moment he drinks it or breaks it is when he steals it from him. And we learned: All robbers pay according to the value at the time of the robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of רבה's rule. It backs it up with a משנה about robbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As long as the barrel exists, the robber's job is just to hand it back, so its price does not matter yet. Destroying it is a fresh act of stealing. Since robbers pay by the value at the moment of stealing, he pays four.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is, in its original form

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Since if it were still there
it would go back to its owner as it is
that moment that he drinks it
or that he breaks it
is when he steals it from him
And we learned
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in בבא קמא (צג:).

phrases.english: All robbers pay
according to the time of the robbery

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כֵּיוָן דְּאִי אִיתַהּ הָדְרָא לְמָרַהּ בְּעֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and supports the first half of רבה's rule from step 18.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's ruling that a robber who breaks or drinks the barrel pays four
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in בבא קמא: כל הגזלנין משלמין כשעת הגזילה, combined with the idea that destroying the item is a new act of stealing

steps.title: Why it breaking by itself costs only one
steps.stepSummary: If the barrel broke by itself, the robber did nothing new to it. He can only be charged for the original robbery, and at that time the barrel was worth one זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it broke by itself, he pays one זוז. What is the reason? Now he did nothing at all to it, so why would you make him pay for now? He pays because of the moment he stole it, and at that moment it was worth only one זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of רבה's rule, where the barrel broke on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is no new act of stealing, because the robber did nothing at the moment the barrel broke. The only thing he can be charged for is the first robbery. So the price is set back at that moment: one זוז.

keyTerms.meaning: He did nothing at all to it

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, the moment that counts is the moment of the robber's act. Destroying the item himself is a new act and sets a new price. If it breaks by itself, only the original robbery counts.

phrases.english: If it broke by itself, he pays a zuz
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא לָא עָבֵיד לַהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי
phrases.english: Now he did nothing at all to it
Why do you make him liable?
It is for that moment that he robbed it
and at that moment it was worth only a zuz

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּבַר מִמֵּילָא מְשַׁלֵּם זוּזָא מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining רבה's rule by giving the reason for the second case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a robber pays only one זוז when the barrel breaks by itself
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He did no new act, so he is charged only for the original robbery, when the barrel was worth one זוז.

steps.title: What does בית הלל's 'time of removal' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to בית הלל's words in the משנה and asks what 'the time of removal' means. It starts with one possible reading: the time the item is removed from the world, meaning destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: בית הלל say, according to the time of removal. What does 'according to the time of removal' mean? If we say it means the time it was removed from the world...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks what בית הלל meant and offers a first reading, which it tests in the next two steps against the rule that all robbers pay by the value at the time of the robbery, and against בית שמאי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Removal' could mean removing the item from the owner's control or removing it from the world. The גמרא tries the second option first: that the שומר pays by the value at the moment the item was destroyed. The next lines will show the problem with this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. It introduces a possible reading that will be tested.
Removal from the world, meaning the item was destroyed or used up

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a final answer. 'אילימא' introduces a suggestion the גמרא is about to challenge.

phrases.english: We learned
Beit Hillel say: according to the time of removal
What does 'according to the time of removal' mean?
If we say: according to the time of removal from the world
phrases.notes: Removed from the world means used up or destroyed, like drinking the wine or breaking the barrel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים כִּשְׁעַת הוֹצָאָה מַאי כִּשְׁעַת הוֹצָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה from step 17 to check it against רבה's rule from step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What בית הלל mean by 'the time of removal'

steps.title: If the item dropped in value, no one says he pays the lower price
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the 'destroyed' reading would be about. If the item lost value before it was destroyed, nobody would let the שומר pay that lower value, because robbers pay by the value at the time of the robbery.
steps.simpleTranslation: In what case are we talking? If the item went down in value, is there anyone who says he pays the lower amount? But we learned in a משנה: All robbers pay by the value at the time of the robbery!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading that 'time of removal' means the time the item is destroyed. This is the first of two possible cases it checks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית הלל meant the time of destruction, then when the value dropped before destruction, the שומר would pay the lower, later value. But a שומר who misuses a deposit is treated like a robber, and the משנה says robbers pay at least the value from when they stole. So no one could hold that he pays less.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case? Which situation are we talking about?
Is there anyone who says so? (meaning no one does)
But didn't we learn in a משנה? (introduces a source that causes a difficulty)
All robbers pay by the value at the time of the robbery

phrases.english: And in what case?
If it is where it decreased in value,
is there anyone who says so?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
All robbers pay
according to the time of the robbery!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמַאי? אִי בְּחָסֵר, מִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר? וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading proposed in step 21, that 'time of removal' means the time the item is destroyed
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of בית הלל's 'time of removal' as the time the item is destroyed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a case where the value went down, this reading would let the שומר pay less than the value when he took the item. That goes against the משנה that all robbers pay by the value at the time of the robbery.

steps.title: If the item rose in value, that is just בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The other case also fails. If the item gained value before it was destroyed and he pays that higher value, this is exactly what בית שמאי say, so בית הלל would not be disagreeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the item went up in value, that is the same as בית שמאי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the second possible case, where the item went up in value, and shows that this case does not work either. Together with step 22, this knocks out the 'destroyed' reading and sets up the need for a new explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי say the שומר pays whichever value is worse for him. When the value rises, the worse value for him is the higher one. If בית הלל also made him pay the higher value at destruction, the two views would be the same, but the משנה presents them as a מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of שמאי, who here say he pays the value that is worse for him

steps.whatToRemember: The reading 'time of removal = when the item is destroyed' fails both ways. If the value dropped, it goes against the robbers' rule. If the value rose, it is the same as בית שמאי.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not rejecting בית הלל's view itself, only one way of explaining his words. The question is what 'time of removal' means, not whether בית הלל is right.

phrases.english: And if it is where it increased in value,
that is the same as בית שמאי!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided challenge begun in step 22 by checking the other case
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of בית הלל's 'time of removal' as the time the item is destroyed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a case where the value went up, this reading makes בית הלל say the same thing as בית שמאי. That would leave no real disagreement in the משנה.
